title: Part Three
html:
The cowherd friends of Vraja. Servants and musicians. The gopis: Gadadhara and Lalita, the eight sakhis and others. The manjaris and the Gosvamis of Vrindavana. Conclusion (verses 124–215)

124"And Arjuna, the son of Pandu, at once became the gopi Arjuniya" — this is clearly stated in the Padma Purana, Uttara-khanda. Therefore the venerable Ramananda Raya is these three.1

The cowherd friends

125Now the devotees from Vraja are named briefly, according to my understanding.

126He who was formerly called Shridama is now the great Abhirama; it was he who carried a log that only thirty-two men could lift.

127He who was formerly called Sudama is now Thakura Sundara;2 and the friend Vasudama is Pandita Sri Dhananjaya.

128Subala, the best of the dear friends, is Gauridasa Pandita; the mighty Mahabala is Kamalakara Pippalai.

129Subahu, a cowherd of Vraja, is Uddharana Datta; Mahabahu, a friend in Vraja, is Sriman Mahesha Pandita.

130The former friend Stokakrishna is Sri Purushottama Dasa.

131The son of Sadashiva named Nagara Purushottama, born in a family of Vaidyas, is Dama, a cowherd of Vraja.

132The former friend named Arjuna is Sri Parameshvara Dasa; Lavanga, a friend in Vraja, is Kala Krishnadasa.

133The brahmana Shridhara Pandita, known as Khola-vecha,3 was in Vraja the jester named Kusumasava.

134The cowherd boy named Prabala, a friend of Balarama, who was formerly in Vraja, is now Halayudha Thakura.

135Krishnachandra's friend in Vraja named Varuthapa is Rudra Pandita, dear to Gauranga.

136Gandharva, a cowherd of Vraja, is Kumudananda Pandita.

Servants, singers and musicians

137The two servants in Vrindavana, Bhringara and Bhangura, were born as the Lord's servants Sri Kashishvara and Govinda.

138The two servants who were formerly in Vrindavana, Raktaka and Patraka, now serve Gauranga: they are Haridasa the Elder and Haridasa the Younger.4

139The two, Payoda and Varida, who formerly prepared the water, are now the servants known as Ramai and Nandai.

140The two singers of Vraja, Madhukantha and Madhuvrata, are Gauranga's singers Mukunda and Vasudeva Datta.

141The former actor Chandramukha is Makaradhvaja Kara.

142He who was formerly in Vraja the mridanga drummer named Sri Sudhakara is now Sri Shankara Ghosha, expert in playing the dampha.

143Chandrahasa, the dancer of Vraja, a knower of rasa, is the lover of dance Sri Jagadisha Pandita.

144He who in Vraja, named Maladhara, held the venu and murali flutes is now the Pandita called Vanamali, dear to Gaura.

145The two famous parrots of Vrindavana, Daksha and Vichakshana, have now been born as my elder brothers, Chaitanya and Ramadasa.5

The gopis, "the potency of the devotee"

146Now, according to my understanding and to what I have heard, are named those of the cowherd women who became dear to the Lord.

147Sri Radha, love personified, formerly the Queen of Vrindavana, is Sri Gadadhara, dear to Gaura, called the Pandita.

148As Sri Svarupa determined, he is the Lakshmi of Vraja:

149"The Lakshmi who was once the beloved of Shyamasundara in Vrindavana is now the Lakshmi of Gaura's love, Sri Gadadhara Pandita."

150Since Lalita follows Radha, being "Anuradhika," she too entered into him, as is said in the Gaura-chandrodaya:

151"This too is Lalita, the friend of Radhika, and not at all this lord of brahmanas, Gadadhara; or else this Hari by His own potency has become threefold: Himself, the friend and Radhika."

152Others have said that Lalita is Dhruvananda Brahmachari; by the distinction of her own manifestations this opinion too is correct.

153Or else Bhagavan Gaura of His own will assumed a threefold form; therefore Sri Gadadhara Pandita is the form of Sri Radhika.

154Chandrakanti, who was a manifestation of Radha's glory, is now near Gauranga as Gadadhara of the Dasa family.6

155Purnananda, who in Vraja was foremost among the beloveds of Baladeva, also entered into this Gadadhara for the sake of the work.

156Chandravali, who once in Vraja was Krishna's supreme beloved, is now in the land of Gauda Kaviraja Sadashiva.

157Sri Bhadra, on whose breast Krishna once slept in Vrindavana, is now Shankara Pandita, dear to Gauranga.

158Sri Taraka and Pali, who were once in the land of Vraja, are now the Lord's dear ones Jagannatha and Sri Gopala.

159Shaibya, who in Vraja was known for her fiery temper, is Damodara Pandita; for a certain purpose the goddess Sarasvati also entered into him.7

160Vishakha, who once in Vraja taught Radha the arts, is now Svarupa Gosvami, who delights in those same moods.

161Chitra, who once in Vraja arranged Radha's hair, is now Kaviraja Sri Vanamali, dear to the Lord.

162Sri Champakalata, who was the very life of Sri Radha in Vraja, is now Raghava Gosvami, who settled at Govardhana, the author of the book Bhakti-ratna-prakasha.

163Tungavidya, who in Vraja was learned in all the shastras, is the renunciant Prabodhananda, the Sarasvati who sings of Gaura.

164Indulekha, who was once Sri Radha's friend in Vraja, is Krishnadasa Brahmachari, who settled in Vrindavana.

165Rangadevi is now Gadadhara Bhatta; Anantacharya Gosvami is she who was Sudevi in Vraja.

166Sri Kashishvara Gosvami is the former Shashirekha in Vraja. Dhanishtha, who in Vraja gave Krishna countless delicacies, is now Raghava Pandita, dear to Gauranga.

167She who in Vraja was Gunamala is Damayanti, his sister; Ratnarekha is Krishnadasa, Kalavati is Krishnananda.

168Shauraseni is the skilful Narayana Vachaspati; Kaveri is Pitambara; Sukeshi is Makaradhvaja.

169Madhavi is Madhavacharya, Indira is Jiva Pandita.

170Sumadhura, who in Vraja was dear to Tungavidya, is Vidya Vachaspati, dear to Gaura and dear to the people of Vraja.

171Balabhadra Bhattacharya is Sri Madhurekshana; Srinatha Mishra is Chitrangi; Kavichandra is Manohara.

172Nandimukhi, who was in Vraja, is now Saranga Thakura. Some consider him Prahlada, but my father does not accept this.

173Kalakanthi and Sukanthi, who in Vraja were in the troupe of the Gandharvas, are Ramananda Vasu and Satyaraja respectively.

174She who in Vraja was Katyayani is now Sri Kanta Sena.

175The overseer of Vraja named Vrinda-devi is now Sri Mukunda Dasa of Khanda, dear to the Lord.

176The messenger Vira, who once in Vrindavana led all the gopis to Krishna, is now my father; she who in Vraja was Bindumati is now my mother.

177Madhumati, once a dear friend in Vrindavana, is now Narahari Sarakara, dear to the Lord.

178The dear friend in Vraja named Ratnavali is Gopinatha Acharya, renowned for his purity.

179The flute, dear to Krishna, is Vamshi Dasa Thakura.8

The manjaris

180Sri Rupa-manjari, who was once famous in Vrindavana, has now appeared, having become Rupa Gosvami.

181Rati-manjari, the dearest friend of Rupa-manjari, is also called by the wise by another name, Lavanga-manjari.

182She is now Sanatana, whose body is non-different from Gaura, worthy of worship by all; for the sake of the work Sanatana, the jewel among sages, also entered into him.9

183Shivananda Chakravarti, who settled in Vrindavana, is renowned as a manifestation of Srimati Lavanga-manjari.

184Ananga-manjari is now Gopala Bhatta; but some call Bhatta Gosvami Sri Guna-manjari.

185Raghunatha Bhatta is the former Raga-manjari. And he who made his dwelling in a hut by Sri Radha-kunda —

186that is Raghunatha Dasa, whose former name is Rasa-manjari; some call him Srimati Rati-manjari, and others, by a difference of names, Bhanumati.

187The former name of Bhugarbha Thakura is Prema-manjari; Lokanatha Gosvami is the former Sri Lila-manjari.

188Kalavati, Rasollasa and Gunatunga, who were in Vraja and sang the songs composed by Sri Vishakha, are now considered to be Govinda, Madhavananda and Vasudeva respectively.10

189Ragalekha and Kalakeli, Radha's maidservants, are to be known as Shikhi Mahiti and his sister Madhavi respectively.

190Malli, the daughter of a Pulinda, has now become Kalidasa.11

191Shuklambara Brahmachari, whose food the Lord Gauranga asked for and ate, was formerly the wife of a sacrificial priest. Some say that the Brahmachari was formerly a brahmana performing sacrifices.

192Other wives of the sacrificial priests are Sri Jagadisha and Hiranyaka, whose food the Lord asked for and ate on Ekadashi.

193Sairandhri, once Krishna's beloved in Mathura, is now Kashi Mishra, who lives in Nilachala, dear to the Lord.

194–207Malati, Chandralatika, Manjumedha, Varangada, Ratnavali, Kamala, Gunachuda, Sukeshini, Karpura-manjari, Shyama-manjari, Shveta-manjari, Vilasa-manjari, Kamalekha, Mauna-manjari, Gandhonmada, Rasonmada, Chandrika, Kalabhashini, Gopali, Harini, Kali, Kalakshi, Nitya-manjari, Kalakanthi, Kurangakshi, Chandrika and Chandrashekhara — all those whom Radha has appointed to the service befitting each — having taken male forms, sported according to their own natures with Gaura and His dear ones, in order as follows: the brahmana Shubhananda; Shridhara Brahmachari; Paramananda Gupta, who composed the Krishna-stavavali; a certain brahmana Raghunatha, who served Gauranga alone; Kamsari Sena; the venerable Sri Jagannatha Sena; Subuddhi Mishra; Sri Harsha; Raghu Mishra, the best of brahmanas; Jitamitra — true to his name, for he conquered and subdued the six enemies headed by lust, and so Gaura named him; Srimad Bhagavatacharya, the author of the booklet Krishna-prema-tarangini, exceedingly dear to Gauranga; the virtuous scholar Sriman Jiva, son of Sri Vallabha; the brahmana Vaninatha of Champahatta, dear to the Lord; Ishana Acharya and Kamala; the Pandita named Lakshminatha; Gangamantri; Jagannatha, called Mamu, the best of brahmanas; Ananta of the Chatta family, called Kanthabharana; Hasti-Gopala; Vallabha of Ranga; Hari Acharya, Gaura's companion; Sri Nayana Mishra; Kavidatta; Ramadasa; Chiranjiva and Sulochana.12

Conclusion

208Some of them are mahantas, others are upa-mahantas; the qualities of both are equal, and therefore I have listed them together.

209Chiranjiva and Sulochana, who live in Khanda, are greater through their companionship with Narahari; their one and only refuge is Gauranga.

210In accordance with the shastra that says, "One should not utter the name of one's guru," I have not revealed the former name of Sri Srinatha.

211He expounded the Bhagavata-samhita with skill; his glory is Krishnadeva, who shines in Kumarahatta.13

212May the mahantas whose order of mention has been broken mercifully forgive me this offence: even Brahma, Shiva and Shesha cannot enumerate all the qualities of the saints.

213This book should be carefully kept hidden from the Mimamsakas, from deceitful logicians and especially from those who delight only in arguments; it should always be given to those versed in the scriptures on rasa who have taken shelter of Gaura's feet.

214This Sri Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika has been composed by me; may it shine in the house of the devotees, filled with the highest bliss.

215In the Shaka year measured by "Vasu" and "Graha," joined with "Manu,"14 on a certain day this book appeared. May the wise, whose hearts are immersed in the nectar of the deeds of Chaitanya-chandra, correct it — this enumeration of Gaura's associates.

Thus ends the Sri Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika, composed by Kavi Karnapura, also known as Puridasa and Paramananda Dasa.

✦

Translator's notes

Notes

  1. That is, three are united in Ramananda: the confidential friend Arjuna, Arjuna the Pandava, and the gopi Arjuniya (Lalita, according to some).
  2. Sundarananda Thakura.
  3. Khola-vecha, "seller of banana bark" (utensils made of banana leaves): the Shridhara of the Chaitanya-bhagavata.
  4. Not to be confused with Haridasa Thakura.
  5. Chaitanya Dasa and Ramadasa, the author's elder brothers, sons of Shivananda Sena.
  6. Gadadhara Dasa.
  7. Chandi, "fiery, sharp-tempered": Damodara Pandita is known for the outspokenness with which he admonished even Mahaprabhu.
  8. Vamshivadana Thakura, by tradition the incarnation of Krishna's flute.
  9. The second "Sanatana" is the sage Sanatana-kumara.
  10. Govinda, Madhava and Vasudeva Ghosha, the brothers who were kirtana singers.
  11. Kalidasa, the uncle of Raghunatha Dasa, known for gathering the food remnants of all the Vaishnavas.
  12. The edition groups verses 194–207 together; the correspondence of the gopis' names to Gaura's associates is given in the order of enumeration.
  13. Srinatha Pandita, the author's guru, wrote the commentary on the Bhagavata called Chaitanya-mata-manjusha and installed the Deity of Krishnadeva in Kumarahatta.
  14. A numerical chronogram: Vasu = 8, Graha = 9, Manu = 14; read backwards, Shaka 1498, i.e. 1576 CE.
